groups.G-container-normalized: A collection built in Sink.__init__ flows only into a consumer that re-normalizes it (a set comprehension / a list comprehension) and is never serialized, never type-inspected, never compared to a tuple literal at the snapshot, so tuple-vs-list produces identical behaviour and output (precedent: SURVIVOR-AUDITS continue_from[89], seal[106], context_pack[40/110]).
groups.G-scan-order: sorted()->list() over a directory scan changes only the order in which (problems, notes) entries are appended; the set of entries, every message, and the verify verdict are identical (precedent: unfinished[2], verify[46], lint[4/5], main[60]).
groups.G-except-OSError-undominated: An except-tuple with OSError dropped: OSError is NOT a subclass of the survivors (ValueError/AttributeError), so unlike SURVIVOR-AUDITS http_transport[17]/reproducer_contract[28] it is no longer caught and DOES propagate. But the sole consumer, verify.verify, wraps the whole re-derivation (review_verify.artifact_problems, diagnostics.artifact_problems, and the budget/delivery/usage re-derivation) in one `except Exception` that appends a 'the record cannot be re-derived' problem, so the top-level verdict is REFUTED whether the inner catch fires or the exception escapes. The OSError branch is also unreachable through anything Sink writes (it only writes regular files, never a directory; the probe-observations dir holds only its own *.json / *.json.tmp).
groups.G-human-read-message-text: A string literal in a (problems|notes) entry is emptied or blanked. The entry is appended regardless of its text, so the verify verdict is unchanged; the text is read only by the operator and parsed by no program and pinned by no test (precedent: main[55/58/62..75] help text, explain[5/31], Reviewer._ocr[139/152/159/166], _closed[9/10], continue_from[153/154] — all AUDITED). 'not harmless' (section 16) is honoured by naming the reader and checking it, not by auto-refuting.

entries.grounds: L144 builds the redaction forms from `(t, json.dumps(t)[1:-1])` for each secret text t: the RAW secret and its JSON-escaped form. Element 0 dropped keeps ONLY the escaped form, so a secret containing a character json.dumps escapes (a quote, a backslash, a non-ASCII letter, a control char) that appears in a probe's detail in its RAW form is no longer redacted and is written verbatim to the artifact file. This violates the module's redaction contract (docstring L34-36: 'Every string in it has the run's secrets replaced ... searched for in the secret's JSON-escaped forms TOO') and leaks a secret. The existing test test_a_secret_is_replaced_in_the_json_part_of_a_text_detail_where_json_wrote_it_escaped (test_v21_pm8_diagnostics.py:340) only exercises the ESCAPED-form path (its detail is `... + json.dumps(facts)`), and the other secrets tests use SECRET='zq9-KEY-7f3a91c2b8' where raw==escaped, so none distinguishes the mutant. Kill-file run: PASS (survives). Reproduced: with secret 'k"ey\\\u00e9-91827364', original _forms holds both forms and redacted() of a raw-form detail returns count=1 (secret absent); the escaped-only forms return count=0 (secret PRESENT).

entries.grounds: L286 `except (OSError, ValueError)` -> `except (ValueError,)` around `json.loads(path.read_bytes().decode('utf-8'))`. OSError is not a subclass of ValueError, so it is no longer caught and propagates out of artifact_problems. The sole consumer is verify.verify (verify.py:175), inside a `try` whose `except Exception` (verify.py:220) appends 'the record cannot be re-derived from the evidence: <type>: <e>'. So: original path -> doc=None -> problems.append('... is not a probe observation ...'); mutant path -> OSError -> verify appends its own problem. Either way problems is non-empty and the verdict is REFUTED. The OSError branch is unreachable through anything Sink writes (regular files only; a directory entry matching _NAME, which would raise IsADirectoryError, is never created), so no measured input reaches it. Not EQUIVALENT (OSError genuinely escapes, with a different message and skipping the later re-derivation), but no consumer depends on the inner catch. Kill-file run: PASS (survives).

exceptions_checked: dominance: OSError NOT a subclass of ValueError, so it is not caught by the survivor (so NOT equivalent-by-hierarchy, unlike http_transport[17]/reproducer_contract[28])

entries.grounds: L275 `if path.name.endswith('.tmp') and _NAME.fullmatch(path.name[:-4])` -> `endswith('')` (always True). For a real .tmp sibling and for a normal .json artifact the behaviour is unchanged (shown below), which is why every kill-file case survives. But a file whose name does NOT end in '.tmp' yet whose name[:-4] matches _NAME — e.g. S1.1.p1.json.bak — is misclassified: original takes the else path and flags it a PROBLEM ('... is not a file this release writes'); mutant matches `endswith('') and _NAME.fullmatch('S1.1.p1.json')` and emits the failed-write NOTE then `continue`. That moves the file from problems to notes, so for a run whose only artifact issue is such a file the verify verdict flips REFUTED -> VERIFIED: verification would silently accept an unexpected file in probe-observations. Not cosmetic (unlike the human-read-text group): it changes WHETHER the file is a problem, which verify.verify's verdict depends on. Kill-file run: PASS (survives). Reproduced: original problems for {S1.1.p1.json, S1.1.p1.json.bak} = ['... S1.1.p1.json.bak is not a file this release writes'], notes = [].

entries.grounds: L315 `present = sum(1 for p in folder.glob('*.json') if p.is_file() and _NAME.fullmatch(p.name))` -> `... if p.is_file() or _NAME.fullmatch(p.name)`. `present` is the count of files this release writes, compared at L316 against RUN.json's `diagnostics.written`; a mismatch is a PROBLEM (or a note under failure). With `or`, present counts any real *.json file even when its name does not match _NAME (and any _NAME-matching directory). Consequences, both verdict-level: (a) a stray real .json file inflates present and FORGES a spurious 'RUN.json states X written, the directory holds X+1' problem; (b) worse, it can MASK a real mismatch — if RUN.json claims 2 written but only 1 real artifact exists alongside one stray .json, original present=1 flags 'holds 1' (correct, REFUTED) while the mutant present=2 equals written and emits NO problem (false VERIFIED). Not cosmetic: `present` exists only for this count check, whose verdict depends on it. Kill-file run: PASS (survives) — no kill-file case puts a stray real .json beside a valid artifact. Reproduced: {S1.1.p1.json, stray.json}: original written=1 -> no count problem; original written=2 -> 'RUN.json states 2 written, the directory holds 1'.

notes: Baseline (unmutated) both kill files PASS, 84 tests. All 12 new mutants were run once each against both registered kill files (tests/v2/test_v21_pm8_diagnostics.py, tests/v2/test_v21_pm8_diagnostics_run.py); all 12 SURVIVE, as expected for campaign-9 survivors. carried: none. Classification: 2 EQUIVALENT (6,7), 7 AUDITED (19,31,64,78,115,121,122), 3 REFUTED (8,47,84). Dividing line used for the string/except mutants, aligned with SURVIVOR-AUDITS precedent: REFUTED only where the mutant changes WHETHER something is a problem (verify verdict can flip: 47, 84) or breaks a hard contract with a security consequence (8, redaction); AUDITED where it changes only the TEXT of an operator-read message that no program parses and the verdict is unaffected (64,115,121,122) or only the order of entries (19) or an unreachable exception branch the sole consumer tolerates identically (31,78). EQUIVALENT reserved for container swaps whose consumer re-normalizes (6,7). The idx 8/47/84 divergences were reproduced directly against the snapshot module (measurement only; no kill file or product code was changed).
